newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 28.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas Corp has halted plans to build its largest and longest-range airliner, the MD-XX, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.
Other top stories included:
- General Motors Corp and the Canadian Automobile Workes union negotiated through a deadline without having reached a definitive agreement on a new labor contract.
- Morgan Stanley could be prevented from underwriting municipal bond deals sold by Massachusetts after one of its senior officials broke rules restricting campaign contributions.
- A surge in aircraft sales helped September durable-goods orders rise 4.6 percent.
- Existing-home sales fell 2.9 percent in September.
- Tele-Communications Inc plans to reduce investment spending and compete against digital-satellite companies.
- Seagram Co Ltd and Viacom Inc cancelled settlement talks, renewing a legal battle over control of USA Network.
- The New York Stock Exchange is considering expanding its trading area.
- The personal computer industry's growth rate slowed to about 16 percent during the third quarter.
- Nationwide Insurance is considering an initial public offering for a 20-percent interest in its life insurance unit.
- Regulators are using a case in Arizona as a model to determine whether municipal bond investors were misled about Miami's finances.
- Federal Express pilots withdrew from the Air Line Pilots Association to create their own collective bargaining agent called FedEx Pilots Association.
- Oracle Corp and Netscape Communications Corp will form an alliance to promote each other's software products.
- Pacific Telesis Group agreed to buy wireless-transmission capacity from an outside carrier to deal with heavy Internet use.
- The U.S. government will launch an on-line service this week to match rich investors with small companies looking for finance.
- A U.S. federal judge gave the former general manager of Daiwa's New York office a two-month prison sentence and a $100,000 fine for his role in hiding $1.1 billion in trading losses by the office.
- Small business groups are worried that the Simple retirement plan they helped get through Congress is going to be too expensive.
- Acuson Corp had $1.6 million in quarterly profit.
- Time Warner Inc said its new media chief will resign at the end of the year.
- The Dow Jones industrial average rose 14.54 points to 6,007.02.

- The conclusion of the $9 billion takeover battle for Conrail Inc could depend on Pennsylvania's tough anti-takeover law, which gives companies a lot of room to reject the highest bid in order to go after a strategic merger.
-- New York Newsdesk 212 859-1610
